baseUrl.description: Issuer. Scheme + host[:port] + optional path, no trailing slash. Every absolute URL the IdP emits derives from this value only.

host.description: Listen address. Also settable with HOST.

port.description: Listen port. Also settable with PORT.

trustProxy.description: Honor X-Forwarded-* from the immediate upstream (true) or from the listed CIDR ranges. Client IP is the rightmost untrusted hop.

trustedOrigins.description: CSRF origin allow-list. Empty by default, which trusts the address each request actually arrived on (its X-Forwarded-Host, or its Host) — what a deployment behind a reverse proxy needs when its public URL is not known at configuration time. Set it to pin the check to named origins instead; `https://*.example.com` matches a subdomain and `*` turns the check off.

allowInsecureHttp.description: Permit a non-https baseUrl outside localhost. Development only.

cookiePath.description: `Path` of every session cookie. Defaults to `/`, so the session is sent to the whole host and a first-party app beside a sub-path deployment shares it. Narrow it to the mount path (`/idp`) to keep the cookie off the other apps on that host — at the cost of any route outside it, the `/gateway` proxy included, no longer receiving the session.

cookieDomain.description: `Domain` of every session cookie. Unset by default, which makes the cookie host-only — the safe default, and what FR-OIDC-14's first-party rule assumes. Set it to a registrable domain (`example.com`) to share the session across that domain's subdomains; every host under it can then read and set the session, so set it only across hosts you control.

secret.description: ≥ 32 random bytes. Fallback env: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET. Must be a placeholder in production.

url.description: Connection string for ordinary application traffic. A transaction-mode pooler belongs here and nowhere else. Optional: when it is absent, `directUrl` serves both roles, which is the single-endpoint deployment (**D74**). Fallback env: DATABASE_URL.

directUrl.description: Direct, non-pooled connection string, used by every step that holds a session advisory lock — startup, migrations, the CLI and the cleanup job — because session locks do not hold through a transaction-mode pooler. This is the connection that must always work; `url` is the optional optimization beside it. At least one of the two must be set, and when `url` looks pooled this one is required. Fallback env: DATABASE_URL_ADMIN.

schema.description: All IdP tables and the drizzle migrations table live here; nothing is created in `public`.

ssl.description: Overrides the connection string's sslmode. Defaults to `require` unless the host is localhost.

poolMax.description: Maximum pooled connections. One instance is the supported topology, so this is the whole deployment's budget.

connectTimeoutSeconds.description: How long a new connection may take before start-up gives up.

name.description: Branding name; also the default TOTP issuer label.

adminTitle.description: What the administration area calls itself, when that is not `site.name` — a deployment whose users think of it as "User Manager" rather than as the identity provider (D61). Branding only: it never reaches the TOTP issuer label, the e-mails or anything a token carries. Defaults to `site.name`.

logo.description: Path under `branding/` or an absolute URL.

favicon.description: As `site.logo`. Both `icon.png` and `branding/icon.png` name the same file (D44).

supportEmail.description: Shown to someone who cannot get in — on the suspended-account page, and in the rejection e-mail.

termsUrl.description: Linked from the sign-up form and the consent screen.

privacyUrl.description: Linked from the sign-up form and the consent screen.

theme.description: `system` follows the browser. The built-in themes are the only ones; there is no custom CSS hook in v1.

nameFormat.description: How a display name is composed from the first and last name that were captured (D49). `first-last` gives "Jane Smith"; `last-first` gives "Smith, Jane". The name itself is never an input field.

apiKey.description: Absent ⇒ degraded mode: every e-mail feature is disabled.

from.description: Required whenever an API key is configured.

replyTo.description: Where a reply goes. Absent, replies go to `email.from`, which is usually a mailbox nobody reads.

enabled.description: Governs password and social registration alike.

allowedEmailDomains.description: Empty = no restriction. Admin-created users always bypass it.

defaultRedirect.description: Where a completed sign-in lands when no OAuth continuation and no validated returnTo apply. Relative path, or an absolute URL when the IdP sits beside the product.

requireEmailVerification.description: Gates password sign-in only. Forced false when e-mail is not configured.

minLength.description: Length is the only strength rule here. Composition rules push people towards P@ssw0rd1 and are not worth the support load.

maxLength.description: An upper bound exists because the hash is computed over the whole value; it is not a strength policy.

breachCheck.description: Check the password against Have I Been Pwned at sign-up and change.

tokenTtlMinutes.description: Reset links expire after this; verification links are fixed at 24 h.

expiresIn.description: How long a browser session lives without being renewed.

updateAge.description: A session older than this is extended on the next request.

cookieCacheMinutes.description: Capped at 5 so revocations bite quickly.

revokeOAuthTokensOnLogout.description: Whether signing out of the IdP also kills the OAuth tokens issued to clients from that session. Off by default: a user closing this tab does not usually mean to sign out of every application they use.

social.description: Keyed by provider id — `google`, `github`, `microsoft`. Each entry needs `clientId` and `clientSecret`; `microsoft` also needs `tenantId`.

clientSecret.description: A `${env:…}` placeholder in production; never a literal.

syncProfile.description: Refresh profile fields from the provider on every sign-in.

allowedEmailDomains.description: Restricts this provider to addresses in these domains. Empty = no restriction.

tenantId.description: Required for `microsoft`: a tenant GUID or verified domain.

enabled.description: Whether users may enroll at all. Enrollment is per user and always optional; turning this off hides the whole feature.

issuer.description: TOTP issuer label. Defaults to site.name.

trustDeviceDays.description: How long a device stays trusted after a successful challenge. `0` asks every time and removes the checkbox.

enabled.description: Off hides the account page and 404s its route.

defaultExpiresIn.description: Pre-filled expiry on the create form.

maxExpiresIn.description: The longest expiry a user may choose.

tokenClientId.description: `azp` of JWTs exchanged from an API key.

tokenTtl.description: Lifetime of a JWT exchanged from a key.

algorithm.description: Neon validates ES256 and RS256 only; any other algorithm is rejected at startup.

audience.description: Default RFC 8707 resource, applied whenever a client sends no `resource` parameter. Becomes the JWT `aud`.

includeUserData.description: Whether access tokens carry the user's name, address and roles at all. Off removes exactly that set.

userClaims.description: Subset selector over {email, name, given_name, family_name, roles}. Defaults to all of them.

claims.description: Static claims merged into access tokens, e.g. `{ "role": "authenticated" }` for Neon/PostgREST.

claimsInIdToken.description: Also merge `jwt.claims` into ID tokens. Off by default: an ID token asserts authentication, and profile data belongs at userinfo.

rotationInterval.description: How often a new signing key is created. The old one keeps verifying for `jwt.gracePeriod`.

gracePeriod.description: Retired keys stay published for this long. Defaults to the longest token lifetime + 1 h.

ttl.description: Lifetime of a JWT from `GET /api/auth/token`, the first-party session exchange.

accessTokenTtl.description: Also the window in which a revoked token still verifies for a stateless resource server.

codeTtl.description: Authorization codes are single-use as well as short-lived.

refreshTokenTtl.description: Sliding: every use rotates the token and restarts this clock.

refreshTokenMaxLifetime.description: The ceiling the sliding window cannot pass. After this the user signs in again.

scopes.description: Every scope any client may request. A client's own `scopes` must be a subset.

resources.description: Extra RFC 8707 resources beyond `jwt.audience` and the per-client ones, each optionally with its own allowed scopes and token lifetime.

prune.description: Delete rows for clients no longer in the file instead of disabling them.

gateways.description: Authenticating reverse proxies, keyed by name: `/gateway/<name>[/<rest>]` streams every method to `<url>/<rest>`. A request carrying `x-api-key` and no `Authorization` has the key exchanged for a session JWT — the same exchange `GET /api/auth/token` performs, with the same ban re-check and the same `azp` — and the JWT is injected as `Authorization: Bearer`, which is what lets a client holding only an API key reach a resource server that validates JWTs against the JWKS. The result is cached for ten minutes, so a revocation takes up to that long to bite unless it goes through this process's admin API. Entries are reconciled into the `gateway` table at start-up under `oauth.reconcile.prune` semantics; rows added on `/admin/gateways` are never touched by that sweep. Each entry is `{ "url": "https://api.internal", "requireAuth": false }`. An upstream reached over plain http receives the minted bearer token in clear.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the upstream, with no trailing slash, query or fragment. `/gateway/<name>/<rest>` is forwarded to `<url>/<rest>`.

requireAuth.description: Refuse a request that carries neither `Authorization`, `x-api-key` nor a session cookie instead of forwarding it anonymously. For an upstream that has no anonymous role of its own.

trustProxy.description: Pass the edge's own `X-Forwarded-For` / `-Host` / `-Proto` through to this upstream instead of replacing them with what this hop can see. Turn it on behind a reverse proxy that sets them — the shipped Caddyfile does — when the upstream needs the browser's address and public URL rather than the container's view of them. **It makes the upstream believe headers this IdP did not write**, so only turn it on when something in front of the IdP overwrites them.

adminRoles.description: Holding any of these opens `/admin` and the admin API. Every name must exist in the role catalog.

allowImpersonation.description: Lets an administrator act as another user, ≤ 1 h, never against another administrator, every action audited.

database.description: `/admin/database`, a schema explorer and SQL console over this deployment's own Postgres. `read-only` runs every statement in a READ ONLY transaction; `read-write` adds a mode toggle and commits when it is set. `disabled` removes the page, the nav entry and both endpoints. One statement per run, 10 s timeout, 500-row cap, every execution audited as `database.queried`. An administrator who can run SQL can read every row at rest — password hashes and session tokens included — so leave it off unless that is intended.

enabled.description: Turning this off removes the rate limits on sign-in, reset, 2FA and the token endpoint. For tests.

storage.description: `database` survives a restart, which is the point of a limit. `memory` is for a single process nobody restarts to get past it.

format.description: `json` for anything that collects logs; `pretty` for a terminal. Also settable with LOG_FORMAT.

intervalMinutes.description: How often the retention job runs: expired sessions, spent verification rows, dead tokens, stale rate-limit rows and retired keys.

retentionDays.description: How long audit rows are kept. They are the answer to what happened, so a short window is a decision, not a saving.
